intro.t: Everybody gets stuck sometimes, and the examiner knows it. What matters is what you do next. Six ways to ask, explain or fix it, and keep going.

close.t: Well done. Getting stuck is normal. Now you know how to get unstuck.

reels.p: Sorry, could you repeat the question?
reels.bt: Sorry, could you repeat the question?
reels.note: Allowed in the exam, and it costs you nothing. Much better than guessing.

ex.q: Is it more important to enjoy your job or to earn a lot of money?
ex.t: {Sorry, could you repeat the question,} please?

ex.q: Should young people learn how to manage money at school?
ex.t: {Sorry, could you} say that again, please?

ex.q: Is it harder to be healthy today than in the past?
ex.t: {Sorry,} I didn't quite catch that. {Could you repeat} it, please?

reels.note: Check, then answer straight away. It shows you are thinking, not lost.

ex.q: Do you think people work too much these days?
ex.t: {Do you mean} adults? I think a lot of them definitely do.

ex.q: Is tourism good or bad for places like islands?
ex.t: {Do you mean} for the people who live there? It's good for jobs, but bad for prices.

ex.q: Why do people like following celebrities?
ex.t: {Do you mean} on social media? I think it's because their lives look exciting.

reels.note: Your first sentence came out wrong? Say it again, more simply.

ex.q: Do you think technology makes people lazy?
ex.t: Sometimes it does. {What I mean is} that we hardly walk anywhere any more.

ex.q: Is it better to have lots of friends or a few close ones?
ex.t: A few, I think. {What I mean is} that close friends matter more than lots of friends.
Partly. {What I mean is} that phones should be off during lessons.

reels.p: I'm not sure of the word, but it's a kind of …
reels.bt: I'm not sure of the word, but it's a kind of…
reels.note: Forgot a word? Describe it. The examiner hears good English either way.

ex.t: It's a flat with a… {I'm not sure of the word, but it's a kind of} small garden on the balcony.

ex.q: What do you like doing on holiday?
ex.t: I love going on… {I'm not sure of the word, but it's a kind of} boat trip along the coast.

ex.q: Is there a sport or hobby you enjoy?
ex.t: Yes, I do… {I'm not sure of the word, but it's a kind of} climbing, indoors, on a wall.

reels.p: Let me put it another way.
reels.bt: Let me put it another way.
reels.note: Shows control. Then give a short, clear version.

ex.q: Is online learning as good as learning in a classroom?
ex.t: Not for me. {Let me put it another way:} I learn better when a real person is in the room.

ex.q: Will robots do most jobs in the future?
ex.t: Some of them. {Let me put it another way:} robots will do the boring jobs, and we'll do the creative ones.
Yes, but… {let me put it another way.} Less homework, but better homework.

reels.note: Everyone makes mistakes. Correcting yourself shows you notice them.

ex.q: How much time do you spend listening to music?
ex.t: About two hours a week… {sorry, I meant} two hours a day!

ex.q: Do you travel far every day?
ex.t: Not really, my school is ten kilometres away… {sorry, I meant} ten minutes away, on foot.

ex.q: Who do you spend time with at the weekend?
ex.t: Mostly with my cousin… {sorry, I meant} my cousins. There are four of them!
